subject: general
question: In which early INC session was the demand first raised for the Indianisation of the higher administrative services, including the civil services?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bombay Session, 1885**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The demand for **Indianisation** of higher administrative services, including the civil services, was first formally raised during the **Bombay Session of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1885**.
 
• This session marked the **foundation of the INC**, which aimed to voice Indian aspirations and seek reforms from the British administration.
 
• One of the key demands during this session was to ensure **greater representation of Indians in administrative services**, as these services were dominated by British officials, leading to a lack of Indian involvement in decision-making processes.
 
• The demand for Indianisation was rooted in the belief that **Indians were equally competent** to serve in higher administrative roles and that their inclusion would lead to more effective governance.
 
• This issue was significant as it highlighted the growing nationalist sentiment and dissatisfaction with British policies that excluded Indians from key roles in governance.
 
• The Bombay Session was presided over by **W.C. Bonnerjee**, the first president of the INC, and laid the foundation for subsequent sessions to address various political and economic grievances.
 
• The demand for Indianisation of administrative services became a recurring theme in the early years of the INC and reflected the aspirations of educated Indians for equal opportunities under British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Allahabad Session, 1890**__

 __
 
• The Allahabad Session of INC in **1890** was presided over by **Pherozeshah Mehta**.
 
• This session focused on broader issues like **economic reforms and self-governance** but did not specifically raise the demand for Indianisation of administrative services.
 
 
 
• **Calcutta Session, 1886**__
 __
 
• The **Calcutta Session of 1886** was significant as it was presided over by **Dadabhai Naoroji**, one of the founding members of the INC.
 
• Although the session addressed issues related to **economic exploitation by the British**, Indianisation was not the central focus.
 
 
 
• **Madras Session, 1887**__
 
 
• The **Madras Session of 1887** was presided over by **Badruddin Tyabji**, the first Muslim president of the INC.
 
• This session was more focused on **unity and communal harmony** among Indians rather than administrative reforms.
